Irregular stems include ser- (be), aur- (have), ir- (go), fer- (do), viendr- (come), prendr- (take) and pourr- (be able). After quand (when) or dès que (as soon as), French uses a future form for future reference, even where English uses a present form. Contrast je partirai (I will leave) with je partirais (I would leave).

outcome: I can join descriptions using qui, que, où and dont.
explanation: A relative pronoun joins a noun to information about it. Qui acts as the subject of the added clause: la femme qui parle means the woman who is speaking. Que replaces a direct object: le livre que je lis means the book I am reading. Où refers to a place or time: la ville où je vis (the city where I live). Dont replaces a de relationship: le livre dont je parle (the book I am speaking about). Choose by the role inside the added clause, not by whether the noun is a person.

explanation: Direct object words le, la and les replace nouns without à. Indirect lui and leur often replace à plus a person; y replaces many à expressions or places, while en replaces many de expressions and quantities. In ordinary statements, the order is me/te/se/nous/vous, then le/la/les, then lui/leur, then y, then en, before the relevant verb. Je le lui donne means I give it to her/him.
